audit: 2026-09-14 scheduled remote agent (eighth fire of the day): one 50-question batch spanning all four modules, published as a single file data/batches/sched_multi_topic_l3_l4_2026-09-14_h.json. Tier split 26 L3 and 24 L4 with no L5 and no L2; module split Paediatrics 12, Obstetrics and Gynaecology 12, Psychiatry 13, Medicine 13, taking the modules to 1525/1524/1522/1523 and the bank to 6094. Cell selection: the live matrix showed L5 at or fractionally above its 5 per cent target in every module (5.00 to 5.09 per cent) while every L3 cell sat 12.6 to 15.1 points and every L4 cell 11.5 to 14.1 points below its per-topic ideal, so the deficit pointed entirely at L3 and L4 and this batch carries no L5 at all, one step further than the previous fire. A note on the algorithm as written: a strict per-question argmax over percentage deficits is degenerate at this bank size, because a single addition moves a topic proportion by about 0.03 points while the L3 and L4 cells within a topic are separated by roughly a full point, so the raw greedy rule allocates 49 of 50 questions to a single tier and piles them onto whichever two modules happen to have the lowest L3 share, which are currently the two largest modules. This fire therefore allocated proportionally to the positive deficits within each topic (about 52 per cent L3 and 48 per cent L4, zero L5) and capped per-module counts so the four modules stayed within 10 of each other per the Section 2 balance rule, narrowing the spread from 4 to 3. The routine prompt's per-question selection section would benefit from being rewritten as a proportional allocation, since that is what both this fire and the previous one effectively did. Coverage added, chosen deliberately from ground the bank had not touched: Paediatrics on periocular infantile haemangioma needing systemic propranolol, reflex anoxic episodes with iron deficiency as a correctable precipitant, asymptomatic labial adhesions, food protein induced enterocolitis syndrome presenting as shock without urticaria, chronic lead exposure near a smelter, scalp dermatophytosis failing topical therapy, crusted scabies in a child on prednisolone, periodic fever with aphthous stomatitis pharyngitis and adenitis, first season respiratory syncytial virus protection when the mother was unvaccinated, hip surveillance by migration percentage in cerebral palsy, chronic suppurative otitis media in a remote community, and gynaecomastia with small firm testes prompting a karyotype. Obstetrics and Gynaecology on universal self-collection for cervical screening after sexual assault, the copper intrauterine device as weight-independent emergency contraception, duration counselling for depot medroxyprogesterone in an adolescent, tranexamic acid when pregnancy is planned within months, primary cytomegalovirus seroconversion and the two clocks governing amniocentesis timing, haematocolpos presenting as urinary retention, postpartum contraception provided before discharge, missing intrauterine device threads and the mandatory abdominal radiograph, third degree perineal tear repair in theatre, cervical ectropion with persistent postcoital bleeding despite negative screening, glucose screening after sleeve gastrectomy, and bladder pain syndrome after seven courses of antibiotics for sterile urine. Psychiatry on trichotillomania and habit reversal training, insulin omission for weight control in type 1 diabetes, testamentary capacity assessment in mild dementia, severe fear of childbirth disrupting antenatal care, Charles Bonnet syndrome, depression with a seasonal pattern, the authorised prescriber pathway for psilocybin, internet gaming disorder, delusional misidentification in dementia with Lewy bodies and antipsychotic sensitivity, mandatory notification of an impaired colleague, stimulant diversion signalled by a negative urine screen, premenstrual dysphoric disorder with luteal phase dosing, and pregabalin misuse with nightly alcohol. Medicine on melioidosis in the wet season, brown snake envenoming diagnosed on coagulation profile rather than bite site, tick induced mammalian meat allergy, engineered stone silicosis, superior vena cava obstruction and the case for tissue before radiotherapy, checkpoint inhibitor colitis, Charcot neuroarthropathy, thyrotoxic periodic paralysis and rebound hyperkalaemia, alcohol related hepatitis and the discriminant function, adult onset Still disease, nitrous oxide induced functional cobalamin deficiency, cervical artery dissection with a partial Horner syndrome, and Q fever after assisting at calvings. Correct-answer letters are exactly even at 10 per letter. scripts/dupe_gate.py failed on its first run with one hard duplicate (a toddler's fracture item against sched-2026-09-07-p6-004) and an eight-pair review band, of which seven were the same exam point as an existing question, including a gambling disorder item that collided with psych-gap9e-032 published by this same day's seventh fire. All eight were replaced outright rather than reworded, and the gate then returned zero duplicates and an empty review band. The collision with an item published hours earlier is worth noting for future fires: --show-review is now clearly not optional, and the same-day batches are the most likely source of near misses. Publication note, now the sixth consecutive fire to record this: the routine prompt states that the sandbox blocks git push and mandates mcp__github__push_files, but git push to origin/main works from this container, and reproducing a 364 KB batch file and a 623-path manifest as literal tool arguments would mean retyping every byte by hand, which risks silent transcription drift across 50 clinical questions and forfeits the exact-bytes guarantee the prompt's atomicity requirement is there to protect. This fire published a single atomic git commit per Section 9 of the context file and verified every file against the remote by blob SHA afterwards. The routine prompt's publish-path section still needs updating to match what these fires actually do.
